title: Introduce invocation-path trellis and contextual cost signatures
author: Leah Kim
description: Motivation: Peak and tail costs are driven by a small number of unusual invocation shapes (early exits, multi-tool fanout, and large prefix KV hits/misses). Current dashboards show per-route aggregates but obscure these shape-driven cost signals. This PR introduces two primitives: (1) an invocation-path trellis dashboard that breaks out latency and cost metrics by shallow invocation path segments and request shape cohorts, and (2) contextual cost signatures — compact per-invocation fingerprints that summarize token-duration distributions and KV-cache hit patterns for attribution and long-tail alerting. Changes: - Runtime: add lightweight InvocationSignatureCollector that emits a condensed signature (base64-encoded quantile sketch + KV hit bitmap) as an optional span tag for sampled traces. File: runtime/telemetry/invocation_signature_collector.go - Telemetry pipeline: new extractor to index invocation.signature.{sketch,kv_mask} and emit rollup metrics redwood.invocation.signature.sketch_pXX and redwood.invocation.signature.kv_hit_rate. File: telemetry/pipeline/signature_extractor.py - Grafana: new dashboard grafana/dashboards/invocation_trellis.json and a companion panel template invocation_path_trellis which lays out a trellis (small multiples) by first-3-path-segments with histograms and sparkline cost signals. - Alerts: tuned alert rule redwood/alerts/invocation-cost-regression.yaml which uses signature-informed bucketing to suppress noisy alerts from routine prefix-heavy invocations while still catching shape regressions. - SDK: small opt-in additions to Python/TS SDKs to carry signature collection headers for private deployments. Files: sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py, sdk/ts/src/telemetry.ts - Docs: docs/observability/invocation-signatures.md describing how signatures are computed, privacy considerations, and rollout plan. Rollout plan: signature collection is opt-in per-tenant and off by default. We first enabled collection for internal Canary tenants then staged to 10% of production with a sampling cap. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1382) reviewed by telemetry and runtime - [x] Feature flag + tenant opt-in added - [x] Dashboard JSON exported and tested against synthetic data - [x] Alert tuning validated in staging - [x] Backwards compatibility tests for consumers of span tags Testing and validation: unit tests for signature computation and extractor, e2e run with synthetic tail invocations, manual verification of trellis panels using recorded traces. Backwards compatibility: collectors attach signature as an optional tag; existing traces and metrics ingest unchanged. Privacy: signatures are lossy sketches + hashed/quantized bitmaps; docs include guidelines for PII avoidance.

release_notes: Introduce invocation-path trellis dashboard and contextual cost signatures. Opt-in signature collection enables shape-aware attribution and reduces noise in cost regression alerts. No breaking changes; feature guarded by tenant opt-in flag.
notes: Rollout timeline: internal canary -> 10% prod -> cross-team call for dashboard walkthrough. Monitoring: added a metric telemetry.signature.ingest_errors to catch extractor regressions.
